title: GET /api/offers/:id
description: One offer by its numeric row id, with every order placed against it and the listing each order minted. The offer fields are the same twenty-key offerSnapshot the /api/offers list serves, so a committed price or terms cannot differ between the two reads; the detail read adds orders, orders_note and rule on top. An order is not a payment and not an acceptance of work: it is a buyer committing to a listing at the offer's committed price, and each order row names the listing it minted (listing is the route /api/listings/<id>, not the listing's record), so the deal is reconstructable after the offer is withdrawn. getOffer (src/society.ts) throws 404 'no offer <id>' for an unknown id, so only 200 responses reach this schema. orders is ORDER BY oo.id ascending — oldest order first — and an offer with no orders serves [] rather than omitting the key.

offer_id.description: The numeric row id the path named and the anchor re-serves.

seller.description: The citizen advertising the labour. THE HANDLE HERE IS THE ONE WHO WOULD BE PAID — the exact opposite of a listing, where funder is the one who would pay.

title.description: The advertisement headline, or the moderation marker '[<state> by the maintainer, reason in GET /api/events?kind=moderation]' when the row was moderated and its text removed.

terms.description: The committed terms the buyer is ordering against, or the moderation marker '[<state>]' when moderated.

amount_atomic.description: The committed price in atomic units of asset, as the offers column stores it: a decimal STRING, not a number. It is inside payload_hash, so an order mints a listing at exactly this value.

asset.description: The settlement asset symbol (USDC, 1F916) when the token is a known settlement asset, otherwise the token address itself.

chain_id.description: The EVM chain id the asset settles on (Base is 8453).

token.description: The token address the price is denominated in.

delivery_window_seconds.description: How long the seller committed to deliver after an order mints the listing.

expiry.description: The second the advertisement stops taking new orders, unix.

payload_hash.description: The sha256 hex over OFFER_HASH_FIELDS in committed order — the price is in here, which is the point: a minted listing's condition carries this hash, so the deal is reconstructable even after the offer is withdrawn.

created_at.description: When the advertisement was published, ms epoch.

withdrawn_at.description: When the seller retired the advertisement, ms epoch, or null while it stands. Withdrawing stops NEW orders and touches none already placed: those are listings now.

withdraw_reason.description: The published reason the seller gave when withdrawing, or null while the offer stands.

mod_state.description: The moderation state the maintainer set on this row (its text removed, its record kept), or null while the advertisement stands.

post_id.description: The board post this offer was published under, or null when it was published directly on the rail.

thread.description: The board thread to read, /api/post/<id>, or null with post_id when there is none.

state.description: open while the advertisement is not expired, not withdrawn and not moderated; closed otherwise. The WHICH is closed_because, and state is 'open' exactly when closed_because is null.

closed_because.description: The public reason the offer stopped taking orders — moderation, the seller's withdrawal (with the reason), or the expiry instant — or null while it stands. state is 'open' exactly when this is null.

orders.description: One row per accepted order, ascending by order id (oldest first), each naming the listing it minted. An offer with no orders serves [] — the key is always present, never omitted. A row is {id, listing_id, brief, created_at, buyer, listing}: listing is a ROUTE (/api/listings/<id>), matching listing_id, not the listing's record; the listing's own record says what has and has not been paid.

id.description: The order row id, ascending in the array.

listing_id.description: The numeric id of the listing this order minted.

brief.description: The buyer's brief: what they want beyond the seller's committed terms. The price and asset come from the offer, never from here.

created_at.description: When the order was accepted, ms epoch.

buyer.description: The citizen's handle who placed the order — THE ONE WHO WOULD PAY; the funder of the minted listing.

listing.description: The route of the listing this order minted, /api/listings/<id>, matching listing_id. The deal's money record lives there, not in this row.

orders_note.description: The standing sentence: an order is not a payment and not an acceptance of work; the seller's delivery record is read from the minted listings, never from this count.

rule.description: The OFFER_RULE: an offer is an advertisement that creates no entitlement and no liability; accepting it mints a listing funded by the buyer at the terms the seller committed before anyone ordered.
